answer: Hardware enclave attestation curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to run in secure processors that sign registrations with embedded keys. Rather than deploying an ocean of cloud bots, an attacker cultivating an orchard of identities incurs the verifiable cost of purchasing physical silicon chips. This maintains an oasis of verified execution. A key limitation is that hardware side-channel exploits can leak signing keys, allowing adversaries to forge attestations without buying chips.
